angle: An octopus has three hearts, blue blood and arms packed with neurons.

claims.verification_notes: DEMO: hand-curated from the Wikipedia 'Octopus' article (circulatory system section). Re-check before publishing.

evidence.quote: Octopuses have three hearts (demo paraphrase, see Circulatory system section)

claims.text: Two of the hearts pump blood through the two gills, and the third (systemic) heart pumps it around the rest of the body.

evidence.quote: two branchial hearts pump blood through the gills; the systemic heart pumps it through the body (demo paraphrase)

claims.text: The systemic heart stops beating while the octopus swims, so it tires quickly and prefers to crawl.

evidence.quote: the systemic heart is inactive when the animal is swimming; it tires quickly and prefers to crawl (demo paraphrase)

claims.text: Octopus blood is blue because it carries oxygen with the copper-rich protein haemocyanin.

evidence.quote: hemocyanin is a copper-containing oxygen-carrying protein that turns blue when oxygenated (demo paraphrase)

claims.text: An octopus has about 500 million neurons, and roughly two-thirds of them are in its arms.

evidence.quote: around 500 million neurons, about two-thirds of them in the nerve cords of the arms (demo paraphrase)

claims.text: Octopus suckers have chemoreceptors, so an octopus can taste what it touches.

evidence.quote: the suckers are equipped with chemoreceptors so the octopus can taste what it touches (demo paraphrase)
